headlines.title: Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia: Long or short accountability?
headlines.summary: Market Hang tackles the top stories of the day. Including Nvidia's board unanimously reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO and what the White House's involvement says about accountability in corporate America, whether the government has effectively put a floor under the AI trade, and Anthropic falling as options on the stock begin trading for the first time. The panel, with Yahoo Finance's Julie Hyman, debates where everyone sits on a one-to-five bullishness scale, whether this is a stock picker's market or a CapEx bubble that precedes a secular bear, the risk of a politically driven slowdown in data center construction, and OpenAI's chief scientist calling for a speed limit on AI development, including whether an FDA-style regulator is the right model for AI.

headlines.title: UPS, FedEx slap $117 holiday surcharge on oversized Christmas packages
headlines.summary: The delivery giants have rolled out their steepest peak-season charges of the year just as Americans prepare to ship Christmas presents.

headlines.title: Missed FedEx's Rally? What Holders Had To Believe
headlines.summary: If FedEx had looked too complex in late 2025, with DRIVE cost savings, Network 2.0 promises, rising labor and environmental pressures, and fresh competition from Amazon’s supply chain push, the decision to buy or wait was not straightforward. Investors who held FedEx over the past year are up 43.8%, including dividends. The question now is which of those early cross-currents really mattered when you weighed that call. FedEx has already moved.

headlines.title: FedEx-led consortium finalizes $9.2B deal for Polish delivery company
headlines.summary: A consortium led by FedEx has completed the takeover of InPost, a large parcel courier in Europe. The post FedEx-led consortium finalizes $9.2B deal for Polish delivery company appeared first on FreightWaves.

headlines.title: Is Wall Street Bullish or Bearish on FedEx Stock?
headlines.summary: FedEx has outperformed the broader market over the past year, and analysts are moderately optimistic about the stock’s prospects.

description: FedEx Corporation, together with its subsidiaries, provides transportation, e-commerce, and business services in the United States and internationally. The company operates through two segments, Express U.S. Domestic and Express International. It provides e-commerce and digital solutions; dataworks; printing and shipping management, including digital printing, professional finishing, document creation, design solutions, direct mail, signs and graphics, custom-branded boxes, copying, computer rental, Wi-Fi, corporate print solutions, shredding, U.S. passport processing and renewal, and digital notarization; packing services, as well as packing supplies and boxes; document and business services; and retail access for package transportation. In addition, the company offers logistics services, air and ocean cargo transportation, specialty transportation, customs brokerage, trade management tools and data, and door-to-door solutions; and third party logistics and supply chain management solutions, such as inbound logistics, warehousing and distribution, fulfillment, contract packaging and product configuration, systems integration, returns process and disposition, test, repair, refurbishment, and product liquidation. Further, it provides sales, marketing, administrative, information technology, and back-office support services. FedEx Corporation was founded in 1971 and is headquartered in Memphis, Tennessee.
